⚡ 🇮🇹 🇩🇪 The Italian branch of Deutsche Bank masked losses amounting to 800 million euros for more than a decade. The irregularities were revealed on Thursday by the British “Financial Times”, citing the results of an internal investigation conducted at the bank. Managers of the Italian subsidiary created a local reserve fund they called “tesoretto” — little treasure chest. This tool was used to conceal the fact that financial targets were not being met. The investigation showed that the branch’s management manipulated falsified provisions for credit losses to create a local accounting pool that hid weak results. The investigation report indicated that the “tesoretto” was used “in order to achieve the profitability of the legal entity.” Profit targets in 2011, 2014 and 2016 were reached thanks to operations involving this hidden financial buffer. The internal investigation, codenamed “Project Aetos”, uncovered irregularities in retail banking and in the management of mortgage credit risk. Deutsche Bank never publicly disclosed the scandal or the findings of this proceeding. The information published by the “Financial Times” forms part of a broader journalistic investigation, “Inside Deutsche Bank”. The project involves the German weekly “Der Spiegel”, German broadcaster ZDF, the American “New York Times” and French “Le Monde”. The revealed facts are based on around 15 million internal Deutsche Bank documents that leaked from the institution. @MedmanNews
